test_cases.then: response body validates against ScanReposResponse — exactly three keys, int types, and as_of_timestamp is ISO-8601 UTC matching the persisted rollup
test_cases.objective: Pin the PRD D-01 assumption: the OpenAPI schema exports the DTO and the runtime body matches it — no extra keys, no missing keys, no non-int counts, no non-UTC timestamp.

test_cases.title: Idempotency: two consecutive successful scans over unchanged repo state produce identical repo counts
test_cases.given: org and probe outcomes are unchanged between two calls
test_cases.then: both responses report the same repos_total and repos_with_harness_installed, and the persisted row equals the last scan's result (last-write-wins semantics tolerated)
test_cases.objective: Prove the scan is idempotent on unchanged upstream state — repo counts do not drift between consecutive scans. The as_of_timestamp is expected to advance and is NOT part of the equality assertion.
preconditions: respx routes are persistent (return the same response for repeated calls)
steps: Mount respx: list-repos → 200 with [repo-a, repo-b, repo-c]
Mount respx: probe repo-a → 200, repo-b → 200, repo-c → 404 (all persistent)
POST /api/admin/scan-repos → capture response body A
POST /api/admin/scan-repos → capture response body B
Read org_summary_rollup row
expected_results: Persisted org_summary_rollup.repos_total == 3 and .repos_with_harness_installed == 2 (equals both response values)
Persisted as_of_timestamp == B.as_of_timestamp (last write wins) and >= A.as_of_timestamp

test_cases.title: Concurrent-rebuild tolerance: endpoint completes 200 while BED-03 rebuild races on the same row
test_cases.given: BED-03's rebuild_org_rollups() concurrently writes to org_summary_rollup during the scan (via an asyncio.create_task before the endpoint call, both against the same test DB)
test_cases.then: the endpoint returns 200 without deadlock or serialization error, per PRD D-02's accepted last-write-wins race
test_cases.objective: Assert the endpoint completes successfully under a racing writer, per the user's brief. Does NOT assert serialization or ordering — either scan or rebuild MAY have the final row and both outcomes are valid.
preconditions: org_summary_rollup seeded with prior real values (repos_total=42, repos_with_harness_installed=17)
Test-scoped rebuild_org_rollups() variant is registered and safe to invoke against the test DB session
steps: Mount respx: list-repos → 200 with [repo-a, repo-b], default_branch='main'
Mount respx: probe repo-a → 200, repo-b → 404
Schedule asyncio.create_task(rebuild_org_rollups(session)) targeting the same org_summary_rollup row
Immediately POST /api/admin/scan-repos
await both tasks
expected_results: No DB-level deadlock / SerializationFailure / IntegrityError is raised

org_summary_rollup singleton row still exists (proves no rollback aborted either writer) — per D-02 no assertion is made on which writer wins or on the final row's `repos_total` value; the earlier claim that `rebuild left repos_total at 42` was factually wrong (rebuild_org_rollups hard-codes `repos_total=0` per BED-03 D-03 because usage_events has no analog for it), and ordering varies between isolated vs full-suite runs so any value assertion would encode timing
